raceSummary.headline: Still no major declarations. Vance is reported to be weighing a pass, and Newsom will decide in early January.
paragraphs: Democrats won both chambers of Congress on Nov. 3, with at least 54 Senate seats and 254 House seats. Republicans are arguing over the cause, with JD Vance blaming the Iran war and Marco Rubio defending it.

CNN reported on Nov. 13 that Vance has seriously weighed not running, though allies still think a run is more likely than not. Rubio gave his first major post-midterm speech to the Federalist Society the same day, and a person familiar with his thinking said he is keeping his options open. Ron DeSantis denied a Washington Post report that he is preparing a bid. Former Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino has had an exploratory committee since June.

On the Democratic side Kamala Harris leads national polls but has not decided. Gavin Newsom, who says he would not run against her, said he will decide in early January. Jon Ossoff, who says he has zero interest in running, won the Crooked Con straw poll with 38.4%.

updates.summary: Candidates: added Gregory Bovino (exploratory committee since June). Vance reported weighing a pass, Newsom set an early-January decision, DeSantis denied a Post report that he is preparing a run, plus new Rubio and Buttigieg moves and a refreshed race summary. Pundits: added Charlamagne tha God (backs a Jon Stewart run, doubts a Harris run), Hasan Piker's September pledge to campaign for AOC, and Steve Bannon's January denial that he is running. No new stances since Nov. 13; November cable ratings are not out yet.

Pundits: added Erick Erickson's Nov. 5 New York Times op-ed criticizing Vance, and Stephen A. Smith's March 2026 leanings toward Marco Rubio and Josh Shapiro. No new stances from the past day; November cable ratings are not out yet.
